extracted.intended_audience: readers and historians of Freemasonry/secret societies and 18th‑century political/religious movements
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted criteria and procedures for admission, noviciate, advancement, obligations, and pedagogy within the Order of the Illuminati as described in a historical account. Includes oaths, observation/reporting requirements, duties, and the Order's aims and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite: prior English three degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates (Minervals) must previously have obtained the three English degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order is accessory to Free Masonry and recruits its Minervals from Masonic lodges; holding the three English degrees is stated as a precondition for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial secrecy oath (pre-conference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before any further conference the candidate must peruse and sign an oath binding himself 'never to reveal, by hint, word, writing, or in any manner whatever, even to my most trusted friend, any thing that shall now be said or done to me respecting my wished-for reception... I promise, that I shall make no intelligible extract from any papers which shall be shewn me now or during my noviciate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This urbanely worded oath is required prior to being introduced to the Illuminatus Dirigens; it explicitly forbids disclosure and extracting information and asserts nothing contrary to religion/state/good manners will be presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: personal table and written questionnaire
rubrics_metrics.description: A candidate fills a 'table' recording name, birth, age, rank, residence, profession, favourite studies, and answers written questions such as 'What advantages he hopes to derive from being a member? What he most particularly wishes to learn? In what respects he thinks he can be of use to the Order? Who are his ancestors, relations, friends, correspondents, or enemies? Whom he thinks proper persons to be received into the Order, or whom he thinks unfit...?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These written answers are used to tailor instruction and to inform Superiors about the candidate's motives, social connections, and suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection by prolonged silent observation
rubrics_metrics.description: After application the candidate is 'carefully observed in silence,' and if thought unfit no notice is taken; if judged suitable, he receives a private invitation to a conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes unobtrusive, extended surveillance of conduct rather than immediate interrogation; lack of notice signals rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novice obligations: reading under mentor, no extracts, weekly written accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Novice must read assigned books in the Mentor's house, must make no extracts, and must give weekly written accounts of his progress; all writings received from Superiors must be returned punctually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned readings include instructions of the Order and delicate questions; weekly reports document progress and are a central part of training and control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescripts: detailed neighbourhood observations to assess character
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the Novice's weekly rescripts must consist of accounts of all interesting occurrences in his neighbourhood, whether public or private; copious narrations of trivial occurrences are especially valued as evidence of character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Superiors use these reports to judge fitness and to discover talents and propensities; remarks on physiognomy and small incidents are prized as revealing true character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary pedagogical aim: self‑knowledge and rooting out prejudices
rubrics_metrics.description: Enlightening the understanding and rooting out prejudices in politics and religion are pointed out as the principal tasks of the noviciate; knowledge of oneself is preparatory to all other knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors disclose a candidate's vulnerabilities and teach by graduated, often delicate discussion; the method includes studying historical characters and scrutinizing local conduct to remove prejudices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time‑bound evaluation: three‑year limit (Sta bene)
rubrics_metrics.description: If three years of the Noviciate elapse without further notice, the Minerval is deemed unfit for advancement and remains a Free Mason of the highest class (a 'Sta bene').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The noviciate is effectively a probationary period of up to three years after which lack of promotion constitutes final non‑selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement obligation: surrender of private judgment and pledge of perpetual loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: On advancement to Illuminatus Minor the candidate must sign an obligation acknowledging his 'natural weakness and inability' and making 'a faithful and complete surrender of my private judgment, my own will' and pledging 'perpetual silence and unshaken loyalty and submission to the Order... to serve it with my fortune, my honour, and my blood.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formal pledge binds the member to place the Order's good above personal ties, to accept discipline and punishment from Superiors, and to align friends/enemies with the Order's determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate readiness for active service and instrumental employment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order 'is not a speculative, but an active association, engaged in doing good to others' and newly advanced members are told they will be 'immediately employed in the service of the Order' and must 'grow wise and able entirely by the unfolding and exertion of his own talents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advancement carries an expectation of prompt deployment: members must accept being used as instruments by Superiors and to perform offices suited to their talents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy enforced by oath and threat
rubrics_metrics.description: Secrecy is enforced: a drawn sword is pointed at the breast and the candidate is threatened with 'unavoidable vengeance' if he betrays the Order; the obligation reiterates perpetual silence and forbids 'secret reservation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond written oaths, physical intimidation and the ritualized threat underline the seriousness of non‑disclosure; making intelligible extracts from materials is expressly prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautious, gradual pedagogical method for controversial doctrines
rubrics_metrics.description: Controversial political and religious doctrines are introduced 'with the utmost caution'; instructors begin with the most easily refutable errors so the pupil 'gets into the habits of victory' and is gradually freed from prejudices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching strategy is incremental: weaken reverence for established systems by tackling simple, refutable points first, then progress to more delicate subjects to avoid alarming timid candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor anonymity and controlled correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Novice knows only his instructor; he may correspond with Provincials/General using addressed forms ('Soli', 'Primo', 'Quibus licet'); 'None but the General and Council know the result of all this' and all are enjoined to keep proceedings unknown to the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymity within chain of command plus regimented, cryptic correspondence preserves internal secrecy while allowing supervised communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on knowledge of human character as core operational skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge of human character is 'of all others the most important' and is acquired by observation, study of historical characters, and continuous rescripts; this knowledge enables members to 'act with men' and to influence conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character knowledge is prioritized over purely scientific instruction for purposes of placement and effective operation within society; it is considered a long‑term, delicate skill with no formal college.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational principle: secrecy to increase zeal and efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Secrecy is identified as a means to increase members' zeal and to allow the Order to 'work silently, and securely'; secrecy binds members and fosters energetic, united action toward the Order's aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text presents secrecy as both a psychological mechanism (enhancing zeal) and a strategic choice to protect activities from external authorities and to accomplish the Order's social/political objectives.
